## Context / Problem

The completion-verifier's repo-materialization path does an attested
`git fetch --no-filter <remote>` bounded by a HARD 300s ceiling
(`src/rebar/_snapshot/git_fetch.py:123` `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300`;
`:247` `--no-filter`; `:281` "attested mode fails closed"). On a large/active
store the unfiltered fetch (every blob of the fetched refs in one RPC) legitimately
exceeds 300s WITHOUT tripping the low-speed abort (data keeps flowing above the
floor), so it fails closed with:

```
Error: git fetch from 'origin' timed out after 300s (attested mode fails closed)
 — the remote may be unreachable or the transfer too large.
```

Observed directly: a standalone `rebar verify-completion 3d7a-7795` died at exactly
300s on this fetch (EXIT 1) — a verdict-less FAULT (neither PASS nor FAIL). The
module docstring itself acknowledges the fetch is "legitimately minutes on a cold
clone" yet caps it at 300s. This is deterministic and O(store) — it is NOT
contention/shared-store load.

Note: this did NOT block the REB-3233 epic close, because that ran in a warm full
clone whose incremental `--no-filter` fetch transferred almost nothing. The fault
manifests on cold/partial clones or when the remote has a large backlog of new
objects since the last fetch — exactly the environments a fresh CI verifier or a
connector-limited agent runs in.

## Resolution

Fixed by Gerrit change 2186 (`rebar-ticket: 8d34-9687-604c-49c8`). The materialization
fetch's wall-clock is now a generous, tunable BACKSTOP rather than the primary guard:
`git_fetch.fetch_timeout()` resolves `REBAR_SNAPSHOT_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` over a scaled
default (`_FETCH_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 3600`) via the owned config seam
(`config.resolve_fetch_timeout`, live per call), applied at both materialization-fetch
sites (`git_fetch.fetch_origin`, `repo_snapshot._ensure_blobs_present`) and the
tightly-coupled sibling `init.py` cold tickets-branch fetch. The throughput-keyed
stall-abort remains the guard against a wedged remote. caused_by: 747f (introduced the
fixed `_GIT_TIMEOUT = 300` cap).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The materialization fetch no longer fails closed purely because a legitimate
  large transfer exceeds a fixed 300s wall-clock ceiling: either the ceiling is
  configurable / scaled, or the fetch is narrowed to only the ref(s) actually being
  materialized (avoiding a full `--no-filter <remote>` of all refs), or the fetch is
  made resumable — with the low-speed stall-abort remaining the guard against a truly
  wedged remote.
- [x] A cold/large-store `verify-completion` (or close-gate materialization) that
  needs a >300s honest transfer completes rather than faulting verdict-less.

## Testing

- [x] A test exercises the materialization-fetch timeout path and asserts the new
  bounding behavior (configurable/scaled ceiling or ref-narrowed fetch), distinct
  from the low-speed stall-abort path, seen RED before the fix and GREEN after.
